title: candidate feedback draft - maya singh (senior SWE, serving runtime)
content:
Quick notes / scratchpad for debrief - Maya Singh (onsite 2026-04-09)
Role: Senior SWE, Serving Runtime
Interviewers: Priya Desai (owner), Alex Kim (system design), Jordan Rivera (coding)
Stage: onsite loop (coding + system design + culture)
Summary (TL;DR): Strong systems background, good latency/cost intuition. Implemented similar KV cache work at prior company. Solid design tradeoffs, coding had a couple of sloppy edge-case misses but fixed after hints. Culture fit seems good - pragmatic, shipping-focused. Recommend: move to manager debrief; leaning hire for IC3/IC4 depending on comp band.

Scorecard (1-5, 5 best)
- Technical chops (algorithms + coding): 4
- System design / infra: 5
- Product sense / latency-cost tradeoffs: 5
- Communication & collaboration: 4
- Ownership & execution: 4
- Overall recommendation: 4 (recommend advance)

Notes by interview:
1) Coding (Jordan) - 60m
- Problem: streaming token aggregator (simplified) + edge-case handling for partial flush/timeout.
- Observations: wrote clean initial solution, used right data structures (deque + counters) but forgot to handle concurrent flush race; corrected after hint. Time management fine. Unit-test ideas were good though didn't write full tests.
- Risk: may need mentoring on defensiveness/edge-case thinking for production-critical infra.
- Strength: concise code, reasonable complexity choices.

2) System design (Alex) - 45m
- Design ask: autoscaling request router + KV cache invalidation semantics for multi-tenant serving.
- Observations: proposed hybrid approach (sharded local cache + central invalidation topic). Good justification for eventual vs strong consistency tradeoffs and tail-latency impact. Suggested batching invalidation acknowledgements to reduce churn.
- Nice: brought up kernel-level considerations (NUMA, memory pinning) when discussing hot-key handling.
- Follow-ups: wants to see concrete metrics to decide sharding scheme (p50/p99 sizes, hotkey skew).

3) Culture / behavioral (Priya) - 30m
- Background: led infra features at previous company (edge inference platform), shipped rollout with canary and automatic fallback.
- Collaboration: examples of cross-team communication (SRE, product).
- Feedback: prefers small iterations, pragmatic tradeoffs. Comfortable with on-call and blameless postmortems.

Strengths:
- Deep infra experience that maps closely to our serving runtime needs (KV cache, batching strategies, autoscaling).
- Strong system-level tradeoff reasoning - cost vs latency conscious.
- Good communicator; can articulate pros/cons succinctly.

Concerns / risks:
- Edge-case defensiveness in coding (missed concurrent flush race initially). Could be mitigated with pairing and code review emphasis early on.
- Not a ton of ML-specific experience (mostly infra). For some product teams we may need someone with model-serving nuances - but for serving runtime infra this is fine.

Comp / Level thoughts:
- Level: IC3/IC4 depending on scope (has ownership + shipped infra features -> IC4 possible).
- Comp: market mid for IC3; justify higher for IC4 if we want ownership of autoscaling/cache subsystems.

Action items / next steps:
- Discuss at hiring committee (manager + eng director) - propose invite to final debrief with hiring manager (Suhail?) and eng director (TBD).
- If moving forward: ask for engineering work sample or short take-home focused on cache invalidation (optional).
- Reference checks: two provided - former manager (email on resume) + tech lead. Priya to run reference check if committee asks.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm willingness to relocate/hybrid (she mentioned prefers SF hybrid) - recruiting to confirm.
- Clarify compensation band expectations - recruiting has notes (see JIRA-RECRUIT-512).
- Follow up on MCQ: had a good answer about NUMA but not deep on GPU memory layouts - relevant if we want someone to also touch quantized kernels.

Links / refs:
- Candidate resume link (internal): CONFLUENCE-8243
- Interview recordings: (internal drive link) - TODO add after upload
- Related ticket: JIRA-RECRUIT-512 (comp + relocation)

Personal notes to self:
- Overall positive - would be a strong add to serving runtime team. If folks are split, push for a short take-home to validate concurrency edge-cases.
- Keep debrief conversational: highlight system design wins (NUMA, batching) and coding miss as low-medium risk.

Draft recommendation language for committee email (short):
"Maya Singh demonstrated strong system-design skills and production infra experience that align closely with our serving runtime priorities (KV caching, autoscaling, tail-latency tradeoffs). Coding was solid, with a minor concurrency edge-case that she resolved after direction. Recommend advancing to manager/comp loop with positive hiring recommendation; consider level IC4 if comp expectations align."

End of draft.

(Notes saved as draft - will clean and move to final after we discuss in debrief.)
